sources_considered.why: Firsthand launch-day tests with described failures and recordings.
Independent launch-day use includes both successful tasks and frustrating interventions.
Independent January 29 testing describes unsuccessful browser research tasks.
Primary underlying-model benchmark results; context rather than a deployed-product success rate.

evidence_items.explanation: The tester reports five failures involving web research and online tools. These show real launch limitations, but the small, relatively demanding task set is not a representative consumer success-rate estimate.

evidence_items.locator: Hands-on review, paragraph introducing the London walking-tour task
evidence_items.explanation: Newton describes successful browser research producing walking-tour links and a completed lesson-plan task. His same review documents substantial shopping friction, so these successes limit the broad dismissal without establishing reliable autonomy.

evidence_items.locator: Section 'When Operator Almost Shines', final paragraph
evidence_items.explanation: This firsthand browser-research test returned unsuitable results despite a lengthy run. The review also describes poor product research, supporting the criticism of practical unreliability.
The underlying model completed substantial shares of benchmark tasks. These company-run evaluations are not measurements of the launch product's reliability for ordinary users.

unresolved_gaps: The independent reviews use small, different task sets rather than a representative shared test.
No speaker-supplied threshold distinguishes 'barely functional' from functional but unreliable.
